title: A tower in fourteen months
summary: From a cleared hotel site to a new skyline, the work moved upward in closely spaced stages.
footnote: Historical milestones; links show selected prerequisites, not the original construction schedule. Today marks the topping-out date.

kinds.label: Site
kinds.detail: Clearing the site and reaching bedrock.

tasks.label: Demolition begins
tasks.detail: Work begins on the old Waldorf-Astoria hotel. The date follows ENR’s construction history.

tasks.label: Excavate the site
tasks.detail: Excavation begins on January 22; foundation work starts on March 17.

risks.label: Work overlaps
risks.detail: Excavation starts before the hotel is fully demolished, requiring careful coordination.

tasks.label: Foundations begin
tasks.detail: Foundation work starts on March 17, the official construction start date.

tasks.label: First upright steel
tasks.detail: The first upright piece of steel is set on April 7.

tasks.label: Raise the steel frame
tasks.detail: From the first upright to the topping out of the main steel frame.

tasks.label: Steel reaches floor 26
tasks.detail: By June 20, the steel has reached the 26th floor.

tasks.label: Main frame tops out
tasks.detail: The main steel frame reaches 1,048 feet on September 19, twelve days ahead of schedule.

tasks.label: Finish the building
tasks.detail: This interval runs from main-frame topping out to opening; it is not a dated record of individual finishing trades.

risks.label: Weak rental demand
risks.detail: The building opens during the Great Depression, when finding tenants is difficult.

tasks.label: Open to the public
tasks.detail: The Empire State Building officially opens on May 1, 1931.
